messages:
emily: heads-up: customer hit a weird rerank failure after we shipped the new batching helper into their mix of services. not a straight pad_to_max story this time.
emily: error snippet from their logs:
```
RuntimeError: rerank: expected all candidate embeddings length 1024 but found [1024, 2048]
also: mismatch between candidate ids and returned scores (index misaligned)
```
raj: index misaligned? did the batcher reorder items for deduping or chunking?
emily: yup. batching helper now performs a dedupe pass to avoid duplicate inputs across a batch. it returned embeddings in deduped order but sampleapp kept the original candidate id order when calling rerank. so even when dims matched, scores were being attributed to wrong candidates; when mixed dims happened we got the hard crash.
sdk-triage: oof. two problems colliding: (1) pad_to_max / model-dim differences across sdks, (2) batcher reorder/dedupe semantic mismatch between helper and caller. we also saw auth retry behavior that re-sent a batch with older padding state, producing dupes with different dims in the same request window.
ops-lee: minimal repro I ran locally:
- start python sampleapp (sdk 0.5.x) -> produces 1024-dim embeddings
- start node sampleapp (sdk 0.8.x with batcher.dedupe=true and pad_to_max=true) -> produces 2048-dim embeddings and reorders outputs
- caller assembled candidate_ids in original order but used reordered embeddings for rerank call -> misattribution + crash when mixed dims exist.
raj: this is painful because the batching helper changed an implicit contract: that the client will receive embeddings in 1:1 order with inputs. we need to decide whether the helper preserves order or the caller must handle mapping back.
emily: short-term mitigation pushed as hotfix: sampleapp now asserts uniform dims and also enforces stable ordering (helper returns an explicit index map). PR link: github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/912. rolled to canary.
ci-bot: sampleapp PR #912 CI passed :white_check_mark:
sdk-triage: long-term fixes:
- change helper API to return {embeddings:[...], order_map:[original_index]} so callers can remap deterministically
- standardize pad_to_max default across sdks (proposal: default=false) and expose embedding_dim in EmbeddingResponse metadata
- rerank endpoint should validate embedding_dim server-side and return structured error EMB_DIM_MISMATCH with a hint about mixed clients/model versions
- add idempotency header to batch endpoints to avoid dupes on auth refresh/retry
raj: also add a small interop e2e in CI that runs node+py sampleapps with dedupe/pad flags mixed and asserts final rerank inputs are well-formed.
ops-lee: I'm adding a support runbook entry showing a short script to check embedding lengths + ordering before calling rerank; will include the assert snippet we used in the hotfix.
emily: customer confirmed canary is green after the hotfix and appreciated the clear error we surfaced. I'll follow up with a brief postmortem and propose the helper API change in RFC.
sdk-triage: assigning follow-ups: RED-DEVEX-1301 (helper API order_map), RED-DEVEX-1302 (embed_dim metadata + sdk parity), RED-DEVEX-1303 (rerank validation & error codes), RED-DEVEX-1304 (batch idempotency)
raj: I'll take 1301 and 1302. adding tests and release note blurb.
emily: thanks team :thumbsup:
